Visit note | 2025-09-02 03:30 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Tuhin Bepari, 71, male. Mr. Bepari comes in reporting a creaking knee and stiffness in the morning for a few minutes. He works as a retired civil servant and notes his symptoms became worse since moving to a building with no lift in Mohammadpur. He has no significant chronic illnesses and denies any recent trauma, locking, or sudden severe swelling in the joint. On examination: BMI 30.6, BP 122/70 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 43 kg. Joint range of motion shows mild crepitus with no significant effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.
